what: On a real crate every test ran on every request (ran=3, cached=0) and no line said why. The sandboxed test server gives no variables, so every trace reads the whole environment as one read named `\0*`; host::answer looked that name up as a variable, answered absent, every settle raced and nothing was kept. The runner read each verdict before the drive that settles it, so the `not kept: raced` was printed as a plain `ok`.
cost: a scenario pass that showed only counts, then a pass reading the path by hand to find the cause
cause: a run's verdict had no reason for running, and the runner could read a verdict at a moment it was not yet final; the host test scripted traces with no whole-environment read and checked verdicts only in the final report
class: a decision whose outcome is reported without its reason, and an outcome read before the step that settles it
prevention: every run's verdict carries why it ran (machine::Missed), on the wire as TestResult::ran and on the line with -v; host::Driver::settled is the one way a runner gets a run's verdict; the host simulation scripts real traces (whole environment included) and checks each settled verdict against the report, with a planted control (Plant::WholeEnvAskedByName)
